description: We are Young Mission Makers,a team of high school students from Vietnam taking part in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We’re curious about how satellite data helps us understand changes on Earth and how astronauts make decisions with limited resources. During the hackathon, we want to use what we learn to build a prototype that addresses a specific problem and makes the science behind it easier to understand.
summary:
Mission Architect is an educational space mission game designed by group of students who are interested and inspired by real NASA missions. Players choose from six missions, design spacecraft by balancing mass, power, data, fuel, and budget, then launch and manage mission events. They also make landing decisions and receive graded reports explaining engineering trade offs and outcomes.

Our project addresses the challenge of making space mission design more engaging and understandable. Instead of learning engineering concepts only through formulas and theory, players experience how different decisions affect a mission in a simulated environment. This is important because it makes complex ideas in spacecraft engineering and systems design more accessible, encourages problem solving, and shows that failure can be a valuable part of learning.
details:
Mission Architect is an interactive space mission design game where players take the role of spacecraft engineers. They choose from six missions, build spacecraft, and balance mass, power, data, fuel, and budget. Players then operate their missions, respond to unexpected events, and receive a final report explaining their performance and engineering decisions.

The game makes complex space engineering concepts easier to understand through hands-on experimentation rather than theory alone. Our goal is to encourage students to explore space science, develop problem-solving skills, and understand the challenges of real space missions.

We developed the game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with the HTML Canvas API for spacecraft visuals, animations, and charts. Its creative approach combines real NASA mission examples with interactive spacecraft design, mission simulations, unexpected events, and performance reports. During development, we considered engineering constraints, scientific objectives, mission risks, safety margins, and limited resources.
